A gynaecologist was put on trial, accused of luring pregnant teenagers with offers of abortion help and holding them until they gave birth; police found four women who had stayed up to three years to bear babies. (The source mentions a deserted building in Uwani but does not say the raid was there.)

20 teenage girls rescued; mothers paid about 20,000 naira; babies sold for 300,000–450,000 naira ($2,500–$3,800)

Placed at the town

06d12ea3c77a98ec.h:
John of God (João Teixeira de Faria) – alleged baby sales from Casa de Dom Inácio de Loyola

Abadiânia, Goiás, Brazil · 2018–2019
John of God's alleged baby farms, BrazilAlleged

In December 2018–January 2019 activist Sabrina Bittencourt (founder of COAME, Combate ao Abuso no Meio Espiritual, working with the victims' group Vítimas Unidas) alleged that João Teixeira de Faria ('John of God') ran, for at least 20 years, a scheme in which poor women near his Abadiânia centre were made pregnant in exchange for food and their babies were sold to foreign families, with his guides and Abadiânia residents as intermediaries. Goiás prosecutors took her statement on 8 January 2019 and São Paulo prosecutors forwarded the material to federal prosecutors; no court has found the baby-sale claims proven, and his lawyer said they lacked evidence. Separately, he was convicted of rapes committed 1986–2017 (19 years 4 months in December 2019; a further 118 years 6 months in September 2023; total sentences reported as 489 years 4 months) and, in November 2019, of illegal possession of firearms (4 years, Abadiânia court). Bittencourt was reported to have died by suicide on 2 February 2019; Brasil de Fato reported Barcelona, Spain, while her son later said Lebanon.

Alleged price per baby US$20,000–50,000 (DOL/Bittencourt) or US$27,000–70,000 (Folha de S.Paulo, cited by AP); prosecutor said alleged sales covered five countries

buyers from United States · buyers from Australia

ec5cd53574107b4b.h:
Lebensborn head office (Munich)

Munich, Bavaria, Germany · 1935–1945
Lebensborn homes and child-Germanization sites, Nazi GermanyHistorical record

Lebensborn e.V. was founded by Heinrich Himmler in December 1935. Its administration was in Munich; from December 1937 to December 1938 the head office was in the villa of the Mann family on Poschinger Straße. Lebensborn leaders Max Sollmann, Gregor Ebner and Günther Tesch were found guilty only of SS membership (count 3) at the 1947–48 Nuremberg RuSHA trial and released on time served; Inge Viermetz was acquitted, and the tribunal found Lebensborn not responsible for the kidnappings.

Births recorded: 1,571 by 31 Dec 1939; 2,400 by 31 Dec 1940; 3,477 by 1 Apr 1942; 5,000 by 30 Sep 1943; 7,000–8,000 in total by 11 May 1945 (de.wikipedia). About 8,000 born in homes in Germany (en.wikipedia); 8,000–9,000 (Planet Wissen); 'etwa 18.000' in all homes (Jüdische Allgemeine). Tribunal found 340 foreign-born children 'handled by Lebensborn e.V.'

Placed at the town

Homes and agencies that sold children (past)Official inquiry finding

83a007427f9f087a.h:
Petland Inc. headquarters

Chillicothe, Ohio, United States · 1967 onward
Shops and brokers selling bred puppiesOperating

Headquarters of Petland, the largest puppy-selling pet store chain in the United States, at 250 Riverside Street, Chillicothe; founded by Ed Kunzelman in 1967. An eight-month HSUS investigation (2008) of 21 Petland stores linked them to puppy mills and brokers, covering more than 17,000 puppies; a 2009 class action alleged sale of unhealthy puppy-mill dogs in at least 20 states. Wikipedia gives 131 US stores in its lead (84 in a later section) and at least 63 abroad (Canada, Japan, China, Mexico, Brazil, El Salvador, South Africa).

21 stores investigated; more than 17,000 puppies traced; puppies sold for up to $3,500 (2008)

Goodman, Missouri, United States · 1991 onward
Shops and brokers selling bred puppiesOperating

Puppy broker founded in 1991 by Andrew Hunte at 121 Roy Hill Blvd, Goodman; described as the largest puppy dealer in the world, buying and selling about 90,000 puppies a year (Tulsa World, 2007) and supplying pet stores including Petland in about 30 US states and exporting to Argentina, Chile, Mexico, Panama, Puerto Rico, Spain and Japan. Puppy broker founded in 1991 by Andrew Hunte at 121 Roy Hill Blvd, Goodman; described as the largest puppy dealer in the world, buying and selling about 90,000 puppies a year (Tulsa World, 2007) and supplying pet stores including Petland in about 30 US states and exporting to Argentina, Chile, Mexico, Panama, Puerto Rico, Spain and Japan. HSUS counted 1,006 puppies on site in March 2015. A 2006 Hunte truck fire in Lowell, Massachusetts killed about 60 puppies; a 2009 class action named Petland and Hunte.

Zhangye hybrid maize seed base

Zhangye, Gansu, China
Where seed is multiplied for the seed companiesReported

2024: about 600,000 mu (about 40,000 ha), >300 million kg of corn seed a year, >40% of China's field corn seed supply; 2021: 46% of field corn seed used nationwide, 450 million kg a year, >800 hybrid varieties
